newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds continue to build on last week's gains.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds continue to build on last week's gains.

text.p: Irish bonds continued to build on their strong gains of last week in thin late trade on Monday as market focus remained on the U.S. ahead of next week's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, dealers said.
Irish bonds surged higher last week, boosted by further foreign buying as well as a well-subscribed tap issue and Thursday's positive Irish inflation data.
"The main thing now is the FOMC meeting in the U.S. on September 24. The market seems to think that there will be a rise in U.S. rates," one dealer said.
Dealers said the market will keep a close eye on August capacity utilisation and industrial production data due out of the U.S. on Tuesday.
U.S. July international trade figures will follow on Wednesday while Thursday sees the release of August housing starts and the September Philadelphia Fed Index.
By 1450 GMT the Irish 8.00 percent bond due 2000 had risen two pence to 104.82 to yield 6.51 percent while the 8.00 percent bond due 2006 had risen 15 to 105.10 to yield 7.13 percent.
Dealers said there were a number of auctions in Europe this week which would be studied carefully by the markets.
Germany will hold a two-year auction on Wednesday, France will auction BTANs on Thursday and Italy will hold an auction of medium and long-term paper on Monday and Tuesday.
The Bundesbank is scheduled to meet on Thursday but dealers said the market does not expect any changes in German rates to be announced.
